brief: A tool rack that hangs on a wall from keyhole hangers, with hooks for small hand tools.

requirements.requirement: Hangs on a wall from keyhole hangers
requirements.evidence: A three-storey keyhole hanger (hex-acc-keyhole-x3) on slot 0, the back face, of the 3-cell column at q0 r0. It placed as accessory:0#0,0#0, 1#0,0#0 and 2#0,0#0, so it hangs on screws already in the wall.
9 hook plates (hex-acc-hook), 2 hooks each, 18 hooks in total. Each level (0, 1, 2) has plates on the front face (slot 3) and the two angled front faces (slots 2 and 4): accessory:L#0,0#2/3/4.
check_build: ok, no errors, meshClash 'clear'. The only note is an info that faces 1 and 5 on each level could take caps.

finish.summary: I built a wall tool rack: a column of 3 cells stacked at q0 r0, with snap joints between levels. A keyhole hanger three storeys tall runs up the back face. Nine hook plates sit on the three front faces of every level, giving 18 hooks for small hand tools. I stacked the cells vertically because a column gives a flat, continuous back face for the hanger. A side-by-side row of hex cells has no flat shared face to mount from. Faces 1 and 5 on each level are still open for caps or more hooks. The checks found no errors and no mesh collisions. This confirms the parts fit, not how much weight the rack can hold.

lines.label: M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
